title: Praise Chore Effort, Not Perfect Folding | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: A ten-year-old's folded towel may not match the neat stack an adult could make in half the time. Refolding everything immediately can turn a contribution into evidence that the child's work was not useful. Pause and decide whether the result is safe and good enough for the skill being learned. Try: You stayed with the whole towel stack and lined up the corners carefully; that effort helped our family. Honest praise for effort and completion supports responsibility while coaching can improve the skill gradually.

claim_limits: Suggested wording is an example, not a guaranteed result.
Adapt expectations to the individual child and safety context.
